Looking at the inner square around rows6-7, cols5-6 with color 3, I check upward extension: for col5, row3 hits a 2 so I fill rows4-5; for col6, row4 hits a 2 so I only fill row5.

Re-examining the earlier example more carefully, I see the ray fill actually operates span-wise across the whole column range rather than per-column — a row is filled only if the entire span is background, and the ray stops as soon as any column in that span hits a non-background cell. That explains why row3 stayed empty in the example even though col7 alone would have kept going.

Applying this to my square at rows6-7, cols5-6: going up, only row5 fills before row4 blocks it; going down, only row8 fills before row9 blocks it; going left, both rows6 and 7 fill at col4 before continuing to check col3.

For the right side, col7 fills for rows6-7 but col8 gets blocked. So this whole cross shape gets filled with color 3.
